title: Akshay and Suniel Are Back in the Same Frame. The Welcome to the Jungle Trailer Is Pure, Glorious Mayhem.
excerpt: A twin-role Akshay Kumar, a Hera Pheri reunion three decades in the making, a Majnu Bhai callback, and a cast so large it needs its own ZIP code. Welcome 3 hits cinemas June 26.
body:
The trailer opens on chaos, and somewhere in the middle of it stands **Akshay Kumar** — twice. Two of him, in fact, because the man is playing a twin role this time, and the entire three-minute promo is built on the comic disaster of compounding misunderstandings. By the time it ends, you've seen explosions, slapstick, a jungle, and a who's-who of Bollywood's comedy royalty crammed into a single frame. This is **Welcome to the Jungle**, the third chapter of the franchise that taught a generation what "controlled chaos" looks like on screen, and it lands in cinemas worldwide on **June 26**.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=C2F0wsBiBvE</youtube>

Let's talk about the moment everyone actually clipped and shared: Akshay Kumar and **Suniel Shetty**, back together, doing the love-hate dance that made *Hera Pheri* a permanent fixture in the desi group chat. Their chemistry is the kind you can't manufacture in a writers' room — it's lived-in, decades-deep, and it crackles the second they share a shot. The trailer knows it, too. It lingers on the pairing like it's the headline act, because it is.

> **"It places him at the centre of it all — and that's a space that has historically produced some of his biggest entertainers." — Trade insider

Directed by **Ahmed Khan** and produced by Firoz A."**

> "Few actors in Hindi cinema have balanced action and comedy as effectively as Akshay Kumar. The trailer doesn't position him as a lone hero. It places him at the centre of it all — and that's a space that has historically produced some of his biggest entertainers." — Trade insider

Directed by **Ahmed Khan** and produced by Firoz A. Nadiadwala, the film leans hard into the film-within-a-film conceit, using Akshay's double act to keep the confusion escalating. There's a knowing throwback baked in for the loyalists — a homage to the legendary Majnu Bhai sequence from the original *Welcome*, the one Anil Kapoor turned into pure meme gold. It's fan service, sure, but the good kind, the kind that lands like an inside joke between the film and everyone who grew up quoting it.

And then there's the cast. Calling it an "ensemble" undersells it. Alongside Akshay and Suniel, you get **Paresh Rawal**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Disha Patani**, **Raveena Tandon**, **Lara Dutta**, **Jackie Shroff**, Johny Lever, Rajpal Yadav, Shreyas Talpade, Tusshar Kapoor, Krushna Abhishek, Kiku Sharda, Daler Mehndi, Aftab Shivdasani — the list keeps going until you start wondering if anyone in the industry *wasn't* called. The Akshay-Suniel-Paresh trio, in particular, is being positioned as the film's beating heart, three comic veterans who could read a phone book and still make you laugh.

![Akshay Kumar — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2a/Akshay_Kumar_National_Award_for_Padman_%28cropped%29.jpg)

There was an emotional note at the trailer launch, too. Akshay grew visibly moved while remembering the late **Pankaj Dheer**, who appears in the film. "Yeh unki aakhri film thi," he said — this was his last film. It's a tender beat in an otherwise raucous campaign, a reminder that behind the spectacle are people, legacies, goodbyes.

Is it high art? Of course not, and it has no interest in pretending to be. This is a big, loud, unapologetic comedy entertainer built for a packed Friday-night hall, the kind of film that works best when the whole row is laughing at once. Akshay Kumar has made a career out of standing dead-centre in the mayhem with a straight face while everything around him detonates, and *Welcome to the Jungle* is him doing exactly that, dialled to eleven.

For the diaspora, the timing is generous. *Welcome to the Jungle* releases in cinemas worldwide on June 26, with overseas distribution across the US, UK, and Canada — expect it on AMC and Cinemark screens in major American metros, Cineworld and Vue in the UK, and Cineplex in Canada, where Bollywood comedies reliably draw a weekend crowd. A streaming home on JioStar is expected down the line, following the franchise's pattern, though no OTT date has been confirmed yet.

The Welcome films have always been about one promise: leave your logic at the door and let the chaos wash over you. On the evidence of this trailer, the third time looks just as gleefully unhinged as the first. Whether it recreates the magic of the original or simply rides its goodwill, one thing is certain — watching Akshay Kumar lose his mind in a jungle, twice over, is going to be a very good time.
